summary: julianday converts a supported date or time value to a fractional day count in the Julian day system.
documentation: julianday converts a supported date or time value to a fractional day count in the Julian day system. Subtracting two values gives an elapsed number of days, making signed calendar-date intervals straightforward.
inputs: spans(id INTEGER, starts TEXT, ends TEXT), containing valid YYYY-MM-DD dates or NULL.
returns: id and days, ordered by id.
caution: The result is a floating-point count of days, not a human calendar description. Local daylight-saving hours are not represented by these date-only intervals.
scenarios: Calculate the calendar-day span of a rental report.
Measure signed schedule slippage between two explicit dates.
Compare dated project milestones across leap days and year boundaries.
title: Measure signed date intervals
problem: Return id and julianday(ends)-julianday(starts) AS days from spans, ordered by id. Equal dates yield zero, reversed dates yield a negative interval, and a missing endpoint yields NULL.
hint: Convert both endpoints before subtracting; do not subtract their text.
goal: Use julianday() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
